We use Taylor's formula in the form

$$
f(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(a)}{3!}(x-a)^{3}+⋯,
$$

with $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $a=-\frac{\pi }{2}.$ 

Computing the required derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ f\,(-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =sin\,(-\frac{\pi }{2})=-1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}\,(-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =cos\,(-\frac{\pi }{2})=0 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {f}^{″}\,(-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-sin\,(-\frac{\pi }{2})=1 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {f}^{‴}\,(-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-cos\,(-\frac{\pi }{2})=0 \\ {f}^{(4)}(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {f}^{(4)}\,(-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =sin\,(-\frac{\pi }{2})=-1. \\ \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =-1+0\,(x+\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{1}{2!}\,{(x+\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+\frac{0}{3!}\,{(x+\frac{\pi }{2})}^{3}+\frac{(-1)}{4!}\,{(x+\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4}+⋯ \\  & =-1+\frac{1}{2}\,{(x+\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}-\frac{1}{24}\,{(x+\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the required derivatives, we have

f(x)=sin⁡xf(−π2)=sin(−π2)=−1f′(x)=cos⁡xf′(−π2)=cos(−π2)=0f″(x)=−sin⁡xf″(−π2)=−sin(−π2)=1f‴(x)=−cos⁡xf‴(−π2)=−cos(−π2)=0f(4)(x)=sin⁡xf(4)(−π2)=sin(−π2)=−1.

Therefore,

sin⁡x=−1+0(x+π2)+12!(x+π2)2+03!(x+π2)3+(−1)4!(x+π2)4+⋯=−1+12(x+π2)2−124(x+π2)4+⋯.
